chapter: Early influences, Oliver date and trombone peers
title: Sending for Red Allen and recording in the 1930s
summary: He sent for Red Allen in New Orleans around 1929-30 and made multiple record dates a day.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: They always talk about your relationship with Little Albert, Red Allen, that you have been associated with-
I sent to him to come to New York.
Where was he? When you sent for him, where was he?
He was in New Orleans.
Do you remember what year?
1929 or 1930 'cause we were playin' because we had a show down there, the Lenox Saratoga Club on 87 Avenue.
On Lenox Avenue in New Orleans?
No ... in New York.
I was getting ready to say there was another Lenox Avenue. And, where did you first hear him, Henry Red Allen?
I didn't hear him in person. I heard his record.
He had made records at that time, the 30s? in 1930
Henry "Red" Allen ... (made) ... a whole lot of records.
Do you remember what label?
I don't know.
Who did he record them with?
Well, different guys -- sometime I'd make two and three different recordings in one day with different bands.
How much were you getting paid a recording? then, about?
I don't know.
Do you have any idea? Ten dollars? How many?
I got mine. Yeah, I got mine, all right. And then Fletcher Henderson ... was playin' with him ... boy, he had a band, too.
